purpose: Gates the regex-based fetchpriority="low" script-tag rewriting filter in includes/class-main.php behind a WP < 6.9 version check so WordPress 6.9+ relies solely on core's native wp_script_add_data( $handle, 'fetchpriority', 'low' ) rendering, retaining the regex filter as a pre-6.9 fallback (with docblock update).
riskRationale: The 6-line code change in class-main.php is small, correct, and verified against WP 6.9's native fetchpriority rendering (Trac #61734 / changeset 60704), with backward compatibility preserved by the retained fallback and its strpos guard. However, the same commit also checks in ~4,737 files / ~525K lines of dev-only Composer dependencies (phpunit, squizlabs/php_codesniffer, wp-coding-standards, mockery, brain/monkey, antecedent/patchwork, nikic/php-parser, sebastian/*, etc.) into the tracked vendor/ directory and flips vendor/composer/installed.php to 'dev' => true, violating AGENTS.md's documented 'composer release' production-only vendor rule, misrepresenting the PR's stated 7-file scope, and shipping dev tooling that .distignore does not exclude in any packaging path that uses the committed vendor.
breakingChanges: No user-facing behavior change. Repository/packaging impact: vendor/ is polluted with dev-only dependencies that are only partially excluded by .distignore, and the new dev autoload_files.php registers PHPUnit/Mockery/brain-monkey global functions on every require of vendor/autoload.php.

text: The functional fix in includes/class-main.php is correct, well-scoped, and factually grounded: WP 6.9 (Trac #61734) is the first core to natively render fetchpriority from wp_script_add_data() extra data, so demoting the regex script_loader_tag filter to a pre-6.9 fallback is exactly right, and the retained strpos guard keeps the gating idempotent on pre-release/RC builds. The blocking problem is repository hygiene: the single commit accidentally bundles ~4,737 dev-only vendor files (~525K insertions) into the tracked vendor/ tree, contradicting the PR's 7-file description and violating the AGENTS.md production-only vendor workflow; two minor robustness gaps (delay-path duplicate attribute, hardcoded version gate with no test coverage) round out the review.

reasoning: The class-main.php change is correct and merge-ready on its own, but the commit must be cleaned: vendor/ must be regenerated production-only via 'composer release' (composer install --no-dev --optimize-autoloader) so only voku/html-min, matthiasmullie/minify, and woocommerce/action-scheduler (plus runtime deps) are committed and installed.php reads 'dev' => false. Optionally guard the delay-JS path against the duplicate fetchpriority attribute newly activated on 6.9+.

message: The version gate is correct and verified against WP 6.9 core: version_compare( $GLOBALS['wp_version'], '6.9', '<' ) keeps the regex fallback active on 6.8.x and below and disables it on 6.9+, matching exactly where core first renders the fetchpriority extra data (Trac #61734). The existing false === strpos( $tag, 'fetchpriority=' ) guard makes the change idempotent even on 6.9 alpha/RC builds where the filter stays registered.

The updated docblock explicitly documents that add_fetchpriority_to_deferred() is now the pre-6.9 fallback only, pointing to the native wp_script_add_data() path in add_defer_strategy(), which captures the intent and future-maintainability of the dual-path design.

add_defer_strategy() sets the native fetchpriority extra data on exactly the same set of handles (non-excluded queued scripts) that the regex fallback covered, so the two mechanisms are behaviorally equivalent across WP versions - a clean architectural handoff that requires no conditional duplication of the registration.

The commit checks in ~4,737 files / ~525K lines of dev-only Composer dependencies (phpunit, squizlabs/php_codesniffer, wp-coding-standards/wpcs, mockery, brain/monkey, antecedent/patchwork, nikic/php-parser, sebastian/*, hamcrest, phar-io, theseer, myclabs, staabm, phpcsstandards, phpcompatibility, dealerdirect) into the tracked vendor/ directory and flips vendor/composer/installed.php to 'dev' => true, while the base branch (2a0bf16e) carried only production packages (voku, matthiasmullie, woocommerce, symfony). AGENTS.md explicitly requires committing vendor/ production-only via 'composer release' (composer install --no-dev --optimize-autoloader); this commit regresses that invariant. The newly committed vendor/composer/autoload_files.php registers PHPUnit assertion functions, Mockery helpers, deep-copy, and brain/monkey API for inclusion on every require of vendor/autoload.php (which Main::includes() does on every request), creating global-function collision risk and runtime bloat. .distignore excludes only squizlabs, wp-coding-standards, dealerdirect, phpcsstandards, bin, and phpcompatibility - so phpunit, mockery, brain/monkey, antecedent/patchwork, sebastian/*, and the rest would ship inside the production WordPress.org ZIP if packaging reuses the committed vendor. The PR lists only 7 changed files but the actual diff is ~4,738 files, a major deviation from stated scope.
suggestion: Run 'composer release' (composer install --no-dev --optimize-autoloader --ignore-platform-reqs), verify vendor/composer/installed.json lists only the three production dependencies, then stage and commit only the production vendor tree together with the class-main.php change. If dev deps are needed for local verification, install them with 'composer dev-setup' but do not commit them. As a belt-and-braces measure, extend .distignore to cover the remaining dev vendor directories.
suggestionCode:
composer release
git reset vendor/
git add vendor/ includes/class-main.php
git commit --amend --no-edit
git status   # confirm no dev packages (phpunit, mockery, brain, antecedent, sebastian, ...) remain staged

message: On WP 6.9+ with both deferJS and delayJS enabled, a delayed handle that is not excluded from defer renders fetchpriority="low" twice: WP 6.9's WP_Scripts::do_item() renders the native attribute from the extra data set at line 1171 before the script_loader_tag filter runs, and add_defer_attribute()'s unguarded str_replace('<script ', '<script fetchpriority="low" ', $tag) then inserts a second attribute, producing invalid duplicate-attribute HTML (browsers use the first occurrence, so functionality is unaffected but the plugin's output is regressed). This is pre-existing code the PR leaves untouched, but the PR is what makes the native path the sole mechanism on 6.9+, so the interplay is newly activated and squarely adjacent to the change's scope.
suggestion: Guard the delay-path fetchpriority insertion with the same false === strpos( $tag, 'fetchpriority=' ) check used by the fallback filter so the attribute is never stamped twice when core renders it natively.

message: This is the only hardcoded version_compare( $GLOBALS['wp_version'], ... ) gate in the codebase; every other 6.9+ feature (lines 358/371) uses function_exists( 'wp_should_output_buffer_template_for_enhancement' ) capability detection, which is more robust because it survives backports and avoids version-string pitfalls. There is no public function to feature-detect classic-script fetchpriority rendering, so a version gate is a reasonable choice here, but $GLOBALS['wp_version'] is read without an isset() guard (safe in a full WP bootstrap, but would emit an 'Undefined array key' warning if setup_hooks() ever runs outside one).
suggestion: Add an isset() guard on the global read and add an inline comment citing Trac #61734 so future maintainers know exactly which core change the 6.9 threshold corresponds to; centralize the boundary as a named helper if a second 6.9 gate is ever needed.

message: The new version-gated behavior (filter registered only when $GLOBALS['wp_version'] < 6.9 and deferJS is enabled) has no automated test coverage: the repo has no PHP unit-test harness wired into CI and the PR adds none, so a regression (e.g. core changing how fetchpriority extra data is rendered, or a wrong boundary) would go undetected. The change's core contract is exactly the kind of regression-prone condition a unit test should lock down.
suggestion: Add a test that sets $GLOBALS['wp_version'] to '6.8' and asserts the script_loader_tag filter for add_fetchpriority_to_deferred is registered when deferJS is on, and repeats with '6.9'/'6.9.1' asserting it is not registered; at minimum, document manual smoke tests on both a <6.9 and a 6.9+ install in the PR body.
